title: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff notes - 2026-07-13
attendees: notes: (some attendees joined late, small gaps in audio)
agenda: Capacity planning for Q3 sales demand
summary: Short meeting to align cross-team priorities for the week. Focus on getting runtime v2.4 canary stable, clear observability gaps discovered during last week's latency spike, and finalize Dedicated capacity plan for new enterprise customer onboarding in mid-August.
notes:
(informal notes, capture decisions and follow-ups)

1) Quick wins / highlights:
- Serving runtime: v2.4 canary showed 12% p99 latency improvement on internal benchmarks for chat workloads. Memory regression observed in long-sequence tests (>=8k) — Marcus and runtime eng to triage.
- Platform: quota billing fix shipped Friday; early telemetry looks good (no billing spikes in 24h).
- Observability: new span tagging merged; will provide better correlation for cache hits/misses in traces.

2) Incidents & oncall review:
- Incident (2026-07-11) - intermittent KV cache invalidation causing token regen for ~3% of requests. Primary cause: race when cache eviction coincided with model switch. Joan summarized RCA draft (linked). Action: temporary mitigation pushed (throttle eviction) fixed immediate regressions. Long-term: revisit cache coordinator design.
- Oncall feedback: need clearer runbook steps for rollback - current steps assume full-service restart which is heavy. Liam to create lightweight graceful-fallback runbook.

3) Runtime rollout status:
- Canary traffic at 5% across us-west and eu-central. No functional errors but the memory regression on long sequences flagged by stress tests. If triage completes this week and no regression found in next 48h, plan to increment to 20% on Monday (2026-07-20).
- Rolling upgrade checklist items pending: automated health checks for per-instance memory and KV-coordinator metrics. Marcus to add two dashboard panels (per-instance mem headroom, eviction rate) by EOD 2026-07-14.

4) Capacity planning (Dedicated + Hosted API):
- Sales forecast: committed trial with AcmeCorp expected to require ~120 sustained tokens/s baseline, burst capacity 450 tokens/s, expected onboarding mid-August. Need guaranteed slots for Dedicated pool or autoscale policy review.
- Finance & SRE ask: create cost estimate for reserved GPU pool vs. burstable hosted for 6 months. Eric to coordinate with finance; target doc by 2026-07-17.

5) Observability & tracing gaps:
- Current gap: inability to attribute per-request cost to batching group reliably in traces. Product wants token-level cost breakdown for a sample of requests to show to customers. Marcus + Hannah to propose approach (sampling + enrichment) by 2026-07-16.
- Note: add synthetic tests for KV-cache behavior under long-sequence chat scenarios. Priya and Marcus to pair.

6) Private deployments readiness:
- Private (on-prem) package: QA found two install-time failures with Debian 12 images (edge-case) — Priya's team has patch queued. Customers in pilot (HealthCo) delayed by one week; need to communicate ETA.
- Compliance: KMS integration checklist almost done; missing audit log shipping validation. Priya to finish by 2026-07-21.

7) Hiring / resourcing:
- Serving Runtime: two backend hires approved; recruiting progressing. Expect one IC onboard by early Aug.
- Observability: contract for telemetry engineer extends to 9/30; need to decide conversion by end of month.

8) AOB:
- Release engineering asked for a freeze-window reminder for next week's minor release to avoid overlap with enterprise onboarding. Liam to publish calendar invite.
- Reminder: leadership offsite planning 2026-08-05 — submit topics (scaling infra, SLOs, hiring) to the shared Confluence page.

Tone/notes-to-self: keep canary incremental, prefer safety over speed for v2.4 rollout. Communicate memory regression transparently to sales/CS to manage expectations.
decisions: Hold 20% canary until memory regression triage complete; target re-evaluation 2026-07-20
Implement temporary throttle for cache eviction as short-term mitigation
Add per-instance memory & eviction dashboards before increasing canary traffic
Create lightweight rollback/runbook for oncall (no full restart)
